meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Хорошо. Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: Fine. So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

examples.text: Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.en: to call, to phone; to ring
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'изойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'происходить'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Подождите! Два дня — это же очень мало.
examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'nowhere', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'football, soccer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Самсон, ты же опаздываешь на футбол!
examples.trans: Samson, you are late for football!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ткнуться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to shut up'.

related.gloss: not to to shut up (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Заткнись, Вика, я никогда не делаю ошибок!
examples.trans: Shut up, Vika, I never make mistakes!

examples.text: Заткнись, рыжая, не мешай мне спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Shut up, redhead, do not disturb me working peacefully!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'садиться'.

examples.trans: He sat down on a chair.
Listen, sit down. Sit down, please.

встать.gloss: to stand up, to get up

meanings.en: to stand up, to get up
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stand up, to get up', paired with 'вставать'.

examples.text: Кто первый встал, того и тапки.
examples.trans: First come, first served (whoever got up first gets the slippers).

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what?
